target_customer: Mobile players of team-based competitive games and the viewers who watch them
problem: Mobile esports were dominated by smaller scale MOBAs. Gamelynx set out to build easily watchable, cross-platform competitive games with fast matches that suit mobile data limits.
business_model: Free to play mobile games, monetization not stated

founders.name: Alexander Mistakidis
education: University of Waterloo (met co-founder as dorm student leaders; degree not stated)
founders.background_notes: GamesBeat says he previously developed League of Legends at Riot Games. The YC page says he later designed characters and gameplay for VALORANT, and he later founded Double Dusk.

founders.name: Carter Minshull
founders.background_notes: GamesBeat describes him as a published physicist specializing in quantum cryptography hacking. The YC page does not list him.

exit.reason: Ceased operations; the cause is not public

competitors.name: Vainglory (Super Evil Megacorp)
competitors.what: Mobile MOBA marketed as the leading mobile esport with organized seasons
competitors.traction_then: Company claimed 3,000 teams and 1 billion matches

technical_complexity.rationale: Building competitive multiplayer games in Unity across mobile and desktop is hard for a small team, but uses standard engines.

defensibility.rationale: A new game gains defensibility only through a player base, and no source shows Gamelynx reached one beyond a claim of more than a million users on a founder profile.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Gamelynx. Tencent's Arena of Valor was cited as precedent and Vainglory was the leading mobile esport.

market_need_then: GamesBeat in May 2018 cited oversaturation of small scale mobile MOBAs and Tencent's Arena of Valor as a precedent for mobile competitive games, showing investor and publisher interest.

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand itself; coverage focused on the funding and the founders' Riot background.

outcome_analysis: Gamelynx was led by a former Riot Games developer and raised about $1.2 million in May 2018 from investors including Riot Games, after a $120K YC seed. A Seedtable profile says it ceased operations in 2020, but no source gives the cause, so failure factors are left empty. The founder later described it as a YC backed studio that reached more than a million users, a self reported figure that did not translate into a sustained business.
notes: No company website is listed, so the site is treated as dead. Round 2 is stated by GamesBeat and PocketGamer.biz (May 18, 2018) and the CB Insights and Seedtable databases; GamesBeat does not give the series. Round 1 rests on Seedtable and BounceWatch. CB Insights shows about $1.35M over 3 rounds and PitchBook about $1.34M, so a small third round is unaccounted for; some aggregators show the $1.2M as debt. A CB Insights page named Gamelynx for a sports betting company is a different entity. The 2020 shutdown date comes from a Seedtable profile seen in search results. The GamesBeat page carries a later update date of 2025.
